Definition: , a prolonged form of a primary εὕρω, which (together with another cognate form) εὑρέω is used for it in all the tenses except the present and imperfect; to find (literally or figuratively):--find, get, obtain, perceive, see.
BiblicalUsage: heurískō is the word for find, get, obtain, perceive, see. I meet it 167 times across the Bible, and Matthew is a good place to see it plainly. It says what it says, and I take it at face value.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe heurískō matters because those who seek Him find Him — God hides from no honest seeker. What I take from it is this — the plain sense is the safe sense.
RelatedEvents: The Angel Appears to Joseph; The Annunciation to Mary; The Calling of the First Disciples
